evidence.note: gitEnv scrubs inherited GIT_* and global/system config for every fixture git, so hook-invoked test runs cannot target the outer repository

AC-4.2..4.9 each have a fixture test: branch scoping across worktrees, rebase, rewrite+rename, stacked inheritance, merged-and-deleted orphaning, name reuse, legacy reachability, --for-branch detached runs, 2,000-run timing, --all emitters never change the exit

regressions for earlier review rounds are pinned: detached-begun rebase, same-named tag, pruned legacy head, ff'd parent head, reused former name, copy-then-delete, unborn branch, stale local main vs origin/main, origin/alice/main not a default branch

doc matches code: branch recorded by fsm init, --for-branch on detached HEAD, merge-base..HEAD range leg, reflog rename leg with the bare-repo caveat, fail-closed git, status --all never changes exit (cmd/metareview/main.go:594, main_test.go:1337)
go test ./internal/status/ passes at head ce80bb4; setup assertions (rebase must rewrite head, rebase must conflict) guard the fixtures against vacuous passes.

findings.note: The rewrite drops the only status-level fixtures for a bare-main repository with linked worktrees (the #174 layout). Branch scoping there relies on the documented no-reflog caveat (known, accepted) and scope-package tests, but no status test exercises DiscoverAbandonedRuns/Build from a worktree of a bare repo, so a regression in common-dir resolution for that layout would only surface in cmd tests if at all. Test-coverage gap, not a behaviour defect.
gitOut uses c.Output(), so a failing fixture git reports only the exit status without stderr (gitRun uses CombinedOutput and prints it). Diagnosability only.
